result: At the pinned rust-sdk v3.1.4 commit, the inspected upstream fixtures do not provide the requested positive handler-side peer_info observation. The mixed-mode fixture establishes a prior 2025-11-25 legacy session and then sends a 2026-07-28 self-identifying request, but that modern request intentionally omits required request metadata and is rejected before another handler dispatch. The positive stateless metadata fixture dispatches tools/list exactly once, but it has no prior initialize context and CountingServer ignores RequestContext. Source inspection further narrows the prior claim: peer_info_for_stateless_request derives protocol_version from the current request/header, but constructs capabilities with ClientCapabilities::default() and client_info with Implementation::default(). Thus current per-request clientCapabilities/clientInfo metadata may be required and validated on the request, but they are not reconstructed into handler peer_info by this source path. The previous unresolved child, as worded, is therefore not satisfied by the inspected fixtures and must be split between current protocol-version peer_info and independently observable request metadata.
source_scope: Own clean LATEST, required sanitized controls, own role config, and two pinned public rust-sdk source/test paths only. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role semantic input, or protected-primary semantic input was used.
scope_guard: Evidence is limited to the pinned source implementation and the named upstream tests. It does not claim deployed-server behavior, authentication or middleware behavior, generic stateful serve_inner behavior, ChatGPT exposure, full MCP conformance, or that handlers cannot observe clientCapabilities through request metadata or another request-context field independent of peer_info.
remaining_unresolved_child: Determine at the same pinned rust-sdk commit whether a handler can observe a modern stateless non-initialize request's non-default _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities through the request or RequestContext independently of Peer::peer_info, since peer_info_for_stateless_request uses default capabilities and client_info.
